config.title: Build reusable notification and toast manager

intro.title: Build reusable notification and toast manager
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable notification and toast manager using JavaScript. You will create a system that can display temporary alert messages (toasts) on a webpage, such as success or error notifications. The core programming concept you'll learn is managing state and using functions to control UI updates dynamically. You'll work with JavaScript functions, DOM manipulation, and CSS for styling to make the notifications appear and disappear automatically. By the end, you'll have a flexible component that can be easily integrated into any web project.
intro.usecase: Notification systems are essential in modern web applications to communicate status updates and user feedback. You'll see toast notifications in e-commerce sites confirming successful purchases, in banking apps showing transaction alerts, and in collaboration tools indicating new messages. As a developer, you'll implement these reusable components to handle success messages, error alerts, and system notifications across dashboards, forms, and user interfaces. This pattern allows consistent user experience while keeping your code DRY and maintainable.

objectives: Construct a reusable notification component with customizable content and styling
Initialize and manage a notification state array to track active messages
Implement functions to add and remove notifications from the state manager
Configure a toast display system that renders notifications based on state
Apply auto-dismissal logic to remove notifications after a specified duration
Integrate user interaction controls to manually dismiss notifications
Manipulate notification positioning and styling through component props

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have React and useState available to use in your notification manager.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the NotificationManager component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named NotificationManager that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called NotificationManager that returns null. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';
// Create the NotificationManager component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A NotificationManager component is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: A function named NotificationManager exists and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'NotificationManager' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named NotificationManager that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize notifications state
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationManager component, use useState to create a state variable called 'notifications' initialized as an empty array.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty array [] as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for a list of items
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'notifications' ready to store notification objects.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an empty array, and the state variable is named 'notifications'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with an empty array [] and naming the state variable 'notifications'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the component, use useState to create a state variable called 'notifications' initialized as an empty array.

steps.title: Create removeNotification handler
steps.instruction: Define a removeNotification function inside your component that takes an id parameter and filters out the notification with that id from the notifications state array.
steps.hint: Use the setNotifications state setter to update the state by filtering the current notifications array. Keep the function inside the component body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a removeNotification function that can be used to delete notifications by their id.
successCriteria: A removeNotification function is defined that takes an id parameter and filters the notifications state array to remove the matching notification.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your removeNotification function takes an id parameter and properly filters the notifications array using setNotifications.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to define a removeNotification function that removes a notification by its id from the state array.

steps.title: Return the component structure
steps.instruction: Return a div container element from the NotificationManager component.
steps.hint: Replace the 'return null;' statement with a return statement that outputs a JSX div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a JSX div element instead of null.
successCriteria: The component returns a JSX div element
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a JSX div element from the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a JSX div element. Check your return statement.

steps.title: Add notification display area
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your NotificationManager component, add a <div> element with a class name 'notification-container' that will serve as the container for displaying notifications.
steps.hint: Add a <div> element with the class attribute set to 'notification-container' inside the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a container div that will hold the notification elements.
successCriteria: A div element with className 'notification-container' is added inside the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a div with the exact class name 'notification-container' inside the return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notification container is missing. Add a div element with className 'notification-container' inside the return statement.

steps.title: Render individual notification items
steps.instruction: Inside the notification display area, map through the notifications state array to render each notification as a div element with its message and apply a CSS class based on its type.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the notifications array. For each notification, return a div with the message text and a className that includes 'notification' and the notification type (e.g., 'success', 'error').
steps.expectedOutcome: Each notification in the state array is rendered as a div element with its message and a CSS class that includes its type, making them visible in the UI.
successCriteria: The notifications array is mapped to render div elements, each displaying the notification message and having a className that includes the notification type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're mapping through the notifications array and applying a className that includes the notification type for each div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notifications are not being rendered correctly. Check that you're using the map method on the notifications array and that each div has the message and a className based on the type.

steps.title: Add close button to notifications
steps.instruction: Inside the notification mapping, add a button element with an onClick handler that calls removeNotification with the notification's id.
steps.hint: The button should be placed inside each notification item. Use onClick={() => removeNotification(notification.id)}.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each notification will have a button that, when clicked, removes that specific notification from the list.
successCriteria: A button element with onClick handler calling removeNotification is added inside the notification mapping.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the button has an onClick handler that calls removeNotification with the notification's id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The close button isn't properly implemented. Check that you've added a button element with an onClick handler inside the notification mapping.

steps.title: Add controls to test the notification manager
steps.instruction: Add a div with the class 'controls' inside the component's return statement, before the notification-container div. Inside this controls div, add three buttons that call addNotification with different message types when clicked.
steps.hint: Place the new div above the existing notification-container. Each button should have an onClick handler that calls addNotification with a message and type (e.g., 'success', 'error', 'info').
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render three buttons (e.g., 'Success', 'Error', 'Info') above the notification area. Clicking each button will add a new notification of the corresponding type.
successCriteria: A div with class 'controls' is added before the notification-container, containing three buttons that call addNotification with appropriate messages and types on click.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some controls, but make sure all three buttons are present and each calls addNotification with a distinct type (e.g., 'success', 'error', 'info').
steps.feedbackWrong: The controls are missing or incomplete. Add a div with class 'controls' containing three buttons that call addNotification with different types.
